claim: Cold is an enhancer of lipid metabolism in peripheral tissues.
source: It has been well documented that cold is an enhancer of lipid metabolism in peripheral tissues, yet its effect on central nervous system lipid dynamics is underexplored.
evidence: Stated as well-documented fact in the abstract

claim: Cold acclimations enhance white adipose tissue lipid lipolysis.
source: It is well recognized that cold acclimations enhance adipocyte functions, including white adipose tissue lipid lipolysis and beiging, and brown adipose tissue thermogenesis in mammals.
evidence: Stated as well-recognized fact in the abstract

claim: Cold acclimations enhance white adipose tissue beiging.
source: It is well recognized that cold acclimations enhance adipocyte functions, including white adipose tissue lipid lipolysis and beiging, and brown adipose tissue thermogenesis in mammals.

claim: Cold acclimations enhance brown adipose tissue thermogenesis in mammals.
source: It is well recognized that cold acclimations enhance adipocyte functions, including white adipose tissue lipid lipolysis and beiging, and brown adipose tissue thermogenesis in mammals.

claim: Cold exposure predominantly increases the expressions of lipid lipolysis genes within the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVH) in male mice.
source: Here, we show that cold exposure predominantly increases the expressions of the lipid lipolysis genes and proteins within the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVH) in male mice.
evidence: Primary finding stated in abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1

claim: Cold exposure predominantly increases the expressions of lipid lipolysis proteins within the PVH in male mice.
source: Here, we show that cold exposure predominantly increases the expressions of the lipid lipolysis genes and proteins within the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVH) in male mice.
evidence: Primary finding stated in abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 2-4

claim: Cold activates cells within the PVH.
source: Mechanistically, by using innovatively combined brain-region selective pharmacology and in vivo time-lapse photometry monitoring of lipid metabolism, we find that cold activates cells within the PVH and pharmacological inactivation of cells blunts cold-induced effects on lipid peroxidation, accumulation of lipid droplets, and lipid lipolysis in the PVH.
evidence: Supported by Fos expression data in Figure 6 and GCaMP6f recordings in Figure 7—figure supplement 1

claim: Pharmacological inactivation of cells blunts cold-induced effects on lipid peroxidation in the PVH.
source: Mechanistically, by using innovatively combined brain-region selective pharmacology and in vivo time-lapse photometry monitoring of lipid metabolism, we find that cold activates cells within the PVH and pharmacological inactivation of cells blunts cold-induced effects on lipid peroxidation, accumulation of lipid droplets, and lipid lipolysis in the PVH.
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 7D showing KYN + MUS treatment prevents cold-induced lipid peroxidation

claim: Pharmacological inactivation of cells blunts cold-induced accumulation of lipid droplets in the PVH.
source: Mechanistically, by using innovatively combined brain-region selective pharmacology and in vivo time-lapse photometry monitoring of lipid metabolism, we find that cold activates cells within the PVH and pharmacological inactivation of cells blunts cold-induced effects on lipid peroxidation, accumulation of lipid droplets, and lipid lipolysis in the PVH.
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 9D showing KYN + MUS treatment prevents cold-induced LD accumulation

claim: Pharmacological inactivation of cells blunts cold-induced lipid lipolysis in the PVH.
source: Mechanistically, by using innovatively combined brain-region selective pharmacology and in vivo time-lapse photometry monitoring of lipid metabolism, we find that cold activates cells within the PVH and pharmacological inactivation of cells blunts cold-induced effects on lipid peroxidation, accumulation of lipid droplets, and lipid lipolysis in the PVH.
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 8D showing KYN + MUS treatment prevents cold-induced lipolysis

claim: PVH lipid metabolism is cold sensitive.
source: Together, these findings suggest that PVH lipid metabolism is cold sensitive and integral to cold-induced broader regulatory responses.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data showing cold-induced changes in PVH lipid metabolism

claim: PVH lipid metabolism is integral to cold-induced broader regulatory responses.
source: Together, these findings suggest that PVH lipid metabolism is cold sensitive and integral to cold-induced broader regulatory responses.

claim: The hypothalamus plays a crucial role in the regulation of systematic energy metabolism.
source: Lipid metabolism in peripheral tissues has been extensively studied, including white adipose tissue lipolysis (Grabner et al., 2021), beiging (Bartelt and Heeren, 2014), and brown adipose tissue thermogenesis Carpentier et al., 2023; however, an essential but poorly understood element is that of lipids in the central nervous system, particularly in the hypothalamus which plays a crucial role in the regulation of systematic energy metabolism (Waterson and Horvath, 2015) and glucose homeostasis (Pozo and Claret, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Waterson and Horvath, 2015

claim: The hypothalamus plays a crucial role in glucose homeostasis.
source: Lipid metabolism in peripheral tissues has been extensively studied, including white adipose tissue lipolysis (Grabner et al., 2021), beiging (Bartelt and Heeren, 2014), and brown adipose tissue thermogenesis Carpentier et al., 2023; however, an essential but poorly understood element is that of lipids in the central nervous system, particularly in the hypothalamus which plays a crucial role in the regulation of systematic energy metabolism (Waterson and Horvath, 2015) and glucose homeostasis (Pozo and Claret, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pozo and Claret, 2018

claim: The brain is highly thermal sensitive in that 1°C or less temperature changes can lead to functional alterations of the central nervous system.
source: The brain is highly thermal sensitive in that 1°C or less temperature changes can lead to functional alterations of the central nervous system (Brooks, 1983; Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Brooks, 1983 and Wang et al., 2014

claim: Lipids provide a major source of energy and heat in the body.
source: Lipids provide a major source of energy and heat in the body, however, the mechanism underlying brain lipid metabolism regulations remains a mystery.

claim: The brain's energy metabolism largely depends on the temperature.
source: There is evidence to show that the brain's energy metabolism largely depends on the temperature (Guyton and Hall, 2006; Yu et al., 2012).

claim: The BODIPY581/591 C11 sensor shifts its fluorescence emission peak from 590 (red) to 510 (green) nm when the sensor is oxidized.

We developed and validated this approach to simultaneously monitor both red and green signals in one brain region through a single implanted photometry fiber connected to a two-color photometry system, for the BD-C11 sensor as it shifts its fluorescence emission peak from 590 (red) and 510 (green) nm when the sensor is oxidized.
